I'm a 19 year old university student who overcame a gambling addiction. AMA
What is it that does it for you? What got you hooked? When I go to a casino with max $100 and when it is gone I leave.

I originally started with small change in high school with friends and then almost a year ago someone introduced me to an online casino. I started to play Texas hold-em and did well but at some point i started to play roulette. As i played i noticed several patterns of how numbers were drawn and started to play based off those. My method worked really well and i took $100 and made over $5000 in a little bit over a week. Then i got overconfident and started to up the amounts i used in the system and at some point i think the system learned how i play by monitoring all my choices. As i started to lose i kept thinking...it's a fluke and i can just turn it all around and start to win again but that's not how it works. i lost all of that and started to put more money into the account thinking....$100 more and i can easily win again etc. when that didn't work i started to put in $200 and $300 at a time and lost it. What hooked me was that i had started to use money from my student loan and i kept on thinking....Oh shit! i NEED to win it back or im fucked. i burned about 4 thousand before i managed to stop. I went to my parents and told them all that had happened and they helped out with my tuition fee and things worked out in the end.
That says a lot about you being able to overcome an addiction like that without needing help. Congratulations!
Thanks. I just hope i never face an opportunity where I might mess up again.

I never thought about how online casinos could have software to monitor (and remember) your gambling patterns and use that against you. For example, knowing you're the kind of gambler who'll take another card at 16 in blackjack.

I cannot confirm whether they actually do or don't but after i had stopped i looked back at my history of hands and what i had chosen and what came out and it was interesting to note that after i had made that original huge winning all of a sudden the pattern that i had used which had NEVER occurred before had started to occur now and then. I wasn't totally clueless to the fact that they had caught on to my system but i was convinced that making new patterns would work to mix it up and win. This worked well short term but after that first pattern was caught they seemed to catch on to any new pattern i used pretty quickly.
What part of gambling had the draw for you?
The main draw is a two edged sword: 1) If I won i got overconfident and thought i could win more and more. 2) If I was losing I felt drawn to not leave on a loss which in turn caused greater loss.
So it arose from the unwillingness to believe that you had the odds against you?
Yes, in a way. It wasn't so much that the odds were with me....it was more that i had a system to beat the odds but i was unwilling to believe that it had been compromised.
Should've pulled a Bringing Down the House.

Now that you mention it I did play Blackjack a couple of times but for very low stakes and I was never really interested in it. I enjoy the game usually but at that point I was fully into the greed phase and if i couldn't win a lot of money quickly i wasn't interested.
This is probably horrible of me for saying this, but you could have gotten a lot of money if you counted cards.

There are two technical problems with this ( excluding any "other" issues with it) 1) Even when counting cards it takes a lot of patience and time and then i was "High" on winning and wanted to continue roulette which got money faster so I only played Blackjack a couple of times. 2) All my playing was online and to count cards it is pretty much imperative to play live because you need to be able to see lots of players cards in order to start counting the deck and measuring the odds. When playing online it is done you and only the computer so to only see two sets of cards per round makes it almost impossible to count cards.
So greed, not the adrenaline rush. I can see how making some quick, easy money is tempting for most people.

To be honest it was a combination of thrill, greed and desperation each having its own phase. Originally it was thrill or adrenaline of finding a way to beat the sytem. Then at some point i realized the money potential and started to get greedy and up the stakes. Then finally at the end was the desperation phase where i was convinced that i need to win it back and that this was the only way to make back the money.
What's the best run you've gone on or seen someone else go on? Not necessarily the amount you/they won but stuff like blackjacks on the trot or hitting 2 times on a 1/36 stuff like that.

My system was (and i advise highly not to try it) based off always doubling my bet when i lost in roulette.So I was betting on RED until black won twice then Black until Red won twice and to keep switching colors after 2 losses for that color. to give more perspective: say my original bet was $2 on red then if i won do the same thing and if i lost then do $4 on red if i won i went back to $2 on red but if i lost then i went to $8 on black etc. So there were no crazy runs but it was a more of a consistent trend. When i was on my initial run at the very end i made about $1500 dollars in one hour....that was the last time i won, after that i went too big and lost a lot.

The main problem was that there was a bet limit of $1000 so when i went to high with the initial bet i wasn't able to double by my losses and ended up losing.
What game/type of gambling? Cards, lottery, etc.

I initially started with sports bets but i had little luck/knowledge to do well there. Then i switched to Texas Hold-em which is my preferred card game and i was doing well there. But once i started to play roulette and the amounts i won there were so much higher I started to see the dollar signs and switched solely to roulette. All online btw.

In my opinion if anyone has the option between playing stuff live or online definitely go with live play. There at least you are holding chips which you can pretend is money to scare yourself into not going crazy. Online there is no such feel and it is easier to lose yourself since there is no tangible connection and it feels more like you are dealing with a cheap commodity than with real money. As well, when playing in a casino you can plan beforehand and only bring x amount and leave all cards and cash far away....online, where all your card info is already there and it takes 3 clicks to get more chips its easier to think that a "little bit" more won't really hurt etc.

Well first, I would like to congratulate you. It must have been really hard to give up such a big thing in your life.

Firstly, I'd like to ask you how you overcame it? Was it through rehab? Friends? Or self-determination? Secondly, why? What was the trigger that forced you to stop? And finally, have you achieved anything afterwards? Like, have you helped others?

And, once again, well done. I have a great deal of admiration for you.

It took self-determination to quit. I didn't consider rehab or counseling or even talking to friends because first of all once i was losing, I didn't want anyone to know. This caused me to both not get help and to continue trying again and again to try and break even. I always told myself that if I break even I'll stop....but in all honesty I doubt I would have. Another reason I quit on my own is that in my mind, at the time, I wasn't addicted....I had a system that didn't work anymore, but if i switch my system (my system is explained above in an earlier reply) then i would win again. While it worked short term it never lasted as long as the original system did and I kept clinging to the notion that the next thing I try will be what works. As for the final trigger.... When i had first started I had used $100 of my own money and after i had started losing I burned through all my personal money (about $800). I was trying to figure out how to get my hands on more money because I was convinced that i could make it all back. I considered various options such as borrowing money from a friend or a bank etc. But then the second half of my student loan for the year was sent out and I suddenly had about $3300. I decided that i could use $200 of it to get back what I had lost before and I started to lose that bit by bit $100 or $200 at a time until at some point i checked my account and there was only about $150 dollars or so in there. I once again thought that I should borrow money to "start the win-streak". At this point the main drive to keep playing was desperation to win back the lost money because I needed it for tuition. When i got a notification that the tuition payments were due soon, I realized that even were I to borrow, I would not be able to win back enough in time, and once I accepted that I started to realize how stupid I had been. I spent a couple of days trying to figure out what to do, whether to tell someone and if so who, and eventually I went to my parents and told them. They took it a lot better than I had thought they would and helped me out with the tuition payment. I then fell into a depression of sorts (I never saw anyone about it so i don't know for sure) during which I didn't want to get up some days, skipped lectures at university and stopped eating some days. This lasted for about two or three months and still hits me sometimes. The problem for me is that I am good at faking being fine and nobody had any idea of what i was going through, and I didn't want to tell my parents because if I were to go see someone, that would be a lot more money wasted because of my original mistake and at that point it was something I couldn't wrap my mind around. Regarding helping others, I haven't told many people about the whole thing yet and only my parents and me know about it. (and now voat lol) but i always keep an ear out and if I ever find out that someone I know wants to play these sorts of games I try to convince them not to do it and if they really want to then not to play online and pull the classic, "I once heard about someone that" ... and say what happened to me.
What would of you done if it wasn't for your parents?

If not for my parents helping me out the only other option that i saw was to attempt to get a tuition fee deferral and attempt to borrow money from either a bank or a friend until i could pay it back working in the summer. If that had not been possible I would have been forced to cancel my semester and would not be able to start again until I had paid the money. But I don't know how I would have handled that outcome.... with my parents helping me out I became depressed...if they hadn't, I don't even want to think about how bad things could have become.

Depression can be a biproduct of debt. Your parents love you. You'll get through this, learn to forgive yourself, pay them back over the years and learn from it. Acknowledge and move on. Go to therapy if need be but don't dwell. Adapt and overcome. The past is the past. Ok that is enough cliches.

I have mostly gotten over the depression and I only get bouts a couple of times a month now which usually last a day or so. I am already working until September semester starts, to pay back my parents. I doubt I will forgive myself until I can be sure that I won't mess up and do it again and until then the past isn't really the past because it could come back to haunt me. How I will know, I don't know, but hopefully as time goes by I'll figure it out.
